subject: QBR prep: trajectory snapshots & three critical unblock requests
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tess Reynolds <tess.reynolds@acmeapps.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: trajectory snapshots & three critical unblock requests

Team — attaching a compact pack for QBR prep (see links & slides attached). Short summary up front so leadership can triage before the deck run: 

Wins:
- Core latency work (KV cache + routing) is now in canary and is reducing median token latency by ~12% in synthetic runs.
- Two enterprise pilots (Acme and BlueHarbor) are on track to increase committed usage in Dedicated by +18% total if no onboarding delays.

Risks (impacting QBR narrative if unresolved):
1) Dedicated onboarding lag: provisioning + security review for Acme is slipping. Blocks revenue recognition timeline (see unblock #A in tracker).
2) Model validation gap: latest open-model quantization shows subtle regression on long-context prompts that could affect product demos.
3) Observability retention: we risk losing 30d traces for some Dedicated customers unless storage tier increase is approved.

Asks (requesting explicit leadership decisions by EOD Thu):
- A: Approve one-time infra credit and expedited security review for Acme (files: unblock-tracker-20260309.xlsx).
- B: Allocate Research 0.5 FTE for two sprints to run extended evals on quantized variants and produce a short risk memo.
- C: Approve temporary increase in trace retention (cost estimate in slides) for Dedicated customers scheduled for go-live in April.

I've attached the short slide set and a tracker with concrete owners and timelines. If we can close A+B by Thursday we can keep the QBR KPIs intact; C is lower revenue risk but high customer trust impact.

Next steps I propose: leadership decision on A/B/C -> we commit plan and owners -> dry run with product/CS on Friday.

Thanks — happy to summarize in the QBR script.

--
Jasmine Liu
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: QBR-trajectory-v2.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: unblock-tracker-20260309.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tess Reynolds <tess.reynolds@acmeapps.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: trajectory snapshots & three critical unblock requests

Thanks Jasmine — solid distillation. A couple quick decisions and clarifying asks: 

1) Approve A (infra credit + expedited security review) conditional on a one-page risk acceptance note from Sales that sets go-live guardrails. Marcus, can Sales produce that by Wed EOD?

2) B (Research support): I approve 0.5 FTE for two sprints, but we need a scoped deliverable (one-page memo + test harness + sample prompts) at the end of sprint 1. Karthik, please prioritize this in the sprint planning and surface any blockers.

3) C (trace retention): Put a conservative estimate for the monthly delta in the slide and route to Finance for a go/no-go — I'll tee up with Finance for fast review.

Also, Jasmine, please add a one-line impact statement per external pilot (Acme, BlueHarbor) on slide 2 — we need a clear dollar impact for the QBR narrative.

I'll join the dry run Friday if the materials are ready.

Laura — yes, Sales can produce the one-page risk acceptance for Acme by Wed EOD. I'll include: go-live guardrails, allowed feature set for initial window, and escalation path.

Action: I'll drop the draft into the shared drive under /QBR/2026/Trajectories by Wed 10:30am.

Also flagging that Finance will need a quick justification note for the trace retention delta — happy to draft a customer-impact paragraph to attach.

Marcus
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Jasmine/Marcus — thanks for the heads up and for pulling the tracker together. A quick update from our side: we can accept the go-live guardrails Marcus will propose, but we do need the expedited security review timeline to be within 7 business days after approval to keep our internal exec commitment.

I've attached a short checklist of our compliance reviewers and their availability. Happy to coordinate a 30-min sync if that helps.

Best,
Tess
Head of Product Ops, Acme Apps
[Attachment: acme-security-checklist.pdf (pdf)]
